info.name: Scintilla
info.comment: Provides advanced text display and editing facilities.

description.p: The Scintilla class provides advanced text editing capabilities that are suitable for modifying text files of any kind, as well as simple user input features for text input boxes. The code is based on the Scintilla project at http://scintilla.org and it may be useful to study the official Scintilla documentation for further insight into its capabilities.

The editor is hosted by a VectorViewport, which is referenced by Viewport and defaults to the Scintilla object's owner. On initialisation the editor creates a View viewport that covers the host and clips the content, and a Page viewport within the View that represents the extent of the document. Scrolling moves the Page within the View, so the View and Page can be passed to a scrollbar such as gui/scrollbar without further integration. The visible text is painted into an internal bitmap that is drawn as the fill of a rectangle within the Page, and only the regions affected by edits, selection changes and scrolling are repainted. The editor follows changes to the size of the host. If the host is freed before the editor, the editor closes its pop-ups and releases its graphics, and operations that display content, such as ShowCompletions, fail with ERR::NotPossible.

Keyboard input and the caret require the user focus, which is monitored through the Focus viewport. The hosting VectorScene must be linked to a Surface for keyboard input, and should have the VPF::IGNORE_TAB flag if the Tab key is to reach the editor.

Text is drawn by the Vector module with the font family in Face at the pixel size in FontSize. Scalable and bitmap faces are supported, and all styles share the same family and size. Lexer styles, margins, the caret, the line highlight and the selection are coloured from the per-editor palette, which is configured in one operation through ThemeXML. Applications that use the GUI packages can build the theme from their GUI palette and reassign it when the palette changes. The editor has no dependency on the GUI packages.

Sizes and positions, including FontSize, LeftMargin, RightMargin, ScrollToPoint and the extent of the Page, are expressed in the units of the View. If the host is scaled, the editor renders at the device resolution: the device scale is taken from all transforms and view boxes that apply to the View, the bitmap is sized in device pixels, and fonts, margins and the caret are drawn at that scale. An editor in a host scaled by 1.5 therefore renders the same pixels as an unscaled editor with a FontSize that is 1.5 times larger, and pointer input is mapped to the same positions. A change of scale, such as zooming the window, reloads the fonts and repaints the editor while retaining the top line and horizontal scroll position. The completion list and call tip are closed by a change of scale. The display density is not applied automatically; applications that use the GUI packages scale FontSize by gui.interface.dpi / 96 as the other widgets do.

Releasing the right mouse button over the editor opens a context menu with Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete and Select All. Items are disabled when they cannot be used: edits require SCIF::EDIT, Cut, Copy and Delete require a selection, and Paste requires text on the clipboard. The menu is displayed with gui/menu at the pointer position, including over a transformed or scrolled host. Closing the menu with Escape or by choosing an item returns the focus to the editor, while moving the focus elsewhere closes it without doing so.

Code assistance is provided through a completion list and a call tip, which the client opens with ShowCompletions and ShowCallTip. The CompletionCallback reports the events that typically prompt them, such as typed characters and Ctrl+Space, as well as accepted and cancelled completions. Only one of the two pop-ups is open at a time. They are drawn above the content of the scene with the editor's font and colours, are positioned at the text that they refer to, and are kept within the bounds of the scene. They follow that text when the editor scrolls, and close if it scrolls out of view. Pop-ups are drawn at the device scale of the host, but are not rotated with it, although their position follows it. Refer to ShowCompletions for the keyboard and pointer interaction.

Drag and drop requires the hosting VectorScene to have VPF::DROP_TARGETS set. The editor registers its visible View as a drop destination. File paths are reported through FileDrop. Text drops insert at the pointer's document position, preserve existing text, convert line endings to the document mode and require SCIF::EDIT.

Dragging selected text within or between editors moves it by default, while Ctrl copies it. Source text is removed only after an editor commits the insertion; dropping onto another kind of widget exports a copy. Native outbound dragging and X11 XDND inbound transport depend on Display support and are separate from these internal operations.

On X11, selecting text publishes it as the primary selection. The middle mouse button inserts the primary selection at that position as one undo action, with document line-ending conversion and read-only enforcement.
The following limitations apply to the current implementation:

list.li: Device scaling applies to scalable faces only. Bitmap faces have fixed sizes, so they are drawn at the size of the View and resampled if the host is scaled.

The device scale is limited to the range 0.5 to 4. Beyond it, and if the host is rotated, skewed or scaled unequally on each axis, the bitmap is resampled. The larger axis scale is used in those cases so that text is never magnified. Lines, such as indentation guides and fold lines, remain one device pixel wide.
A modifier key that is pressed while the application window does not have the keyboard focus is not known to the editor until it is pressed again.
Rectangular clipboard content is recognised only within the process that copied it. Refer to Clipboard for details.
Primary selection is supported only by the X11 display driver.
If the Page is moved a large distance by a third party, such as a scrollbar, the previous content can be shown for one frame before the editor repaints.

action.name: Clear
action.comment: Clears all content from the editor.

action.name: Clipboard
action.comment: Cut, copy and paste text through the system clipboard.

input.param: The mode that will be used to shift data between the target object and clipboard system.

description.p: The Clipboard action provides the same cut, copy and paste operations as the editor's key bindings (Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Shift+Del, Ctrl+Ins and Shift+Ins). Text is exchanged as UTF-8 through the Clipboard class. The editor also binds Ctrl+L to cut the lines that the selection touches, and Ctrl+Shift+T to copy the current line.

CLIPMODE::COPY copies the selection. CLIPMODE::CUT copies the selection and deletes it, but only once the clipboard has accepted the text. Nothing is copied if the selection is empty. A rectangular selection is copied with a line ending after each row, and is pasted as a rectangle when it is pasted into a Scintilla editor in the same process.

The clipboard carries plain text without a rectangular marker, so the editor recognises a rectangular clip by comparing the pasted text with the most recent rectangular copy in the process. Consequently, identical text that is later copied from another source is also pasted as a rectangle, and a rectangular copy from another process or application is pasted as ordinary text.
CLIPMODE::PASTE replaces the selection with the most recent text on the clipboard, as a single undo action. Line endings are converted to the document's line ending mode.

If Flags does not include SCIF::EDIT, cut and paste are refused with ERR::ReadOnly and reported as SEF::FAIL_RO. If the clipboard cannot be read or written, the error is logged and reported as SEF::FAIL_CLIPBOARD.

result.error: The operation completed, or there was nothing to copy.
The Mode is not supported.
The clipboard holds no text to paste.
The resource has not been initialised

method.name: AddMarker
method.comment: Adds a marker to a line.
method.prototype: ERR sci::AddMarker(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, INT Marker)

input.param: The index of the line.
The marker number, from 0 to 24.

description.p: A marker is a symbol that is drawn in the symbol margin beside a line, or a highlight of the line's text, as configured by DefineMarker. Markers are typically used to indicate bookmarks, breakpoints and errors. The symbol margin is enabled with Symbols. While it is hidden, a line that carries markers is highlighted with their background colour instead.

There are 25 markers, numbered from 0 to 24. A line can carry any combination of them, and adding a marker that the line already carries has no effect. A marker stays with its line as text is inserted and deleted. If the line is joined to the previous line, the markers of both lines are combined.

method.name: BeginUndoAction
method.comment: Begins a client undo group.
method.prototype: ERR sci::BeginUndoAction(OBJECTPTR Object)

description.p: BeginUndoAction() starts a group of edits that Undo and Redo will treat as a single step. Every edit made until the matching call to EndUndoAction is added to the group, whether it originates from the client or the user.

Groups can be nested. Each call must be balanced by a call to EndUndoAction, and the group is closed only when the outermost call is ended. Open groups are preserved when new content is loaded, and any groups that remain open when the Scintilla object is freed are closed automatically.

result.error: Operation successful.
The maximum nesting depth has been reached.
The resource has not been initialised
The editor is dispatching a notification and cannot be modified until it returns.

method.name: ClearIndicator
method.comment: Removes an application indicator from a byte range.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ClearIndicator(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Indicator, INT Start, INT End)

input.param: An indicator slot previously defined with DefineIndicator.
Byte offset of the first byte to clear.
Byte offset immediately after the last byte to clear. Must be between Start and TextLength.

description.p: ClearIndicator() removes the marks of an indicator slot from the bytes in the range Start to End, leaving the marks of other slots untouched. Marks that extend beyond either end of the range are trimmed rather than removed, so clearing the middle of a run leaves two separate runs. To remove every mark in a slot, clear the range from zero to TextLength.
The slot must have been defined with DefineIndicator. Clearing a range does not modify the document, its undo history, DocumentRevision or the selection.

result.error: Operation successful.
Indicator has not been defined.
Indicator is outside the range 8 to 31, or the byte range is invalid.
The resource has not been initialised

method.name: CollapseFold
method.comment: Collapses a fold without toggling its current state.
method.prototype: ERR sci::CollapseFold(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line)

input.param: Zero-based document line, or -1 for the caret line.

description.p: Collapses the fold that starts at Line, hiding its child lines. If the line does not start a fold, the innermost fold that contains it is collapsed. The states of nested folds are retained and apply again when the fold is expanded with ExpandFold. Collapsing a fold that is hidden within a collapsed ancestor records its state without expanding the ancestors. Collapsing a fold that is already collapsed succeeds without change.
Unlike ToggleFold, the result does not depend on the fold's current state. Folding must be enabled with FoldingMarkers, and the document needs a Lexer that supports folding.

result.error: Operation successful.
Folding is disabled, or the line has no fold containing child lines.
A value is outside of the valid range
The resource has not been initialised
Operation cannot complete because system is busy with an earlier operation
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: Colourise
method.comment: Restyles a range of the document with the active lexer.
method.prototype: ERR sci::Colourise(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Start, INT End)

input.param: Byte offset at which to start styling.
Byte offset at which to stop styling. Must not be less than Start or greater than TextLength.

description.p: Colourise() runs the active Lexer over the range Start to End immediately. The lexer may begin styling from an earlier position if it needs preceding context to resolve the range correctly.

Calls to SetKeywords and SetLexerProperty invalidate the existing styles, but the affected text is not restyled until it is next drawn. Call Colourise() after such changes when the updated styles are needed straight away. To restyle the entire document, use a range of zero to TextLength. An empty range is accepted and has no effect.
Styling does not modify the document, its undo history or DocumentRevision.

result.error: Operation successful.
The byte range is invalid.

method.name: ConvertEOLs
method.comment: Converts existing line endings as one undo operation.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ConvertEOLs(OBJECTPTR Object, SCEOL Mode)

input.param: The line-ending representation to apply to existing text.

description.p: Converts every CR, LF and CRLF sequence in the document to the representation given by Mode, including documents with mixed line endings. The conversion is recorded as a single undo action, so one Undo restores the original bytes. It can also be nested inside a BeginUndoAction group. A document that is empty or already uses Mode throughout is left unchanged and no undo step is created.

This method does not alter EOLMode, which controls the line endings of subsequently entered text. Set both to normalise a document and keep it consistent. Conversion is a programmatic edit, so it does not require the EDIT flag in Flags. It is reported through ChangeCallback and advances DocumentRevision like any other edit.
The document length is checked before any text is modified, so a failed conversion leaves the content unchanged.

result.error: Operation successful.
Mode is invalid, or the converted document would exceed the maximum document length.
The resource has not been initialised
The method was called from within a synchronous editor notification.

method.name: DefineIndicator
method.comment: Defines the appearance of an application indicator slot.
method.prototype: ERR sci::DefineIndicator(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Indicator, SCIND Style, INT Colour)

input.param: The application slot to define, from 8 to 31.
The visual style of the indicator.
An explicit 0xRRGGBB colour, or a theme reference from -1 to -3.

description.p: Indicators annotate ranges of document text without altering the text or its lexical styling, and are typically used to highlight diagnostics such as compiler errors, warnings and search matches. DefineIndicator() configures the appearance of a slot so that it can be applied to text with FillIndicator and ClearIndicator.

Slots 8 to 31 are available to applications. Lower slots are reserved for lexers and higher slots for input method composition. Indicators are drawn beneath the text, and each slot is drawn independently so that overlapping ranges remain visible. The available styles are:
The Colour is either an explicit colour in 0xRRGGBB format or one of the following theme references, which follow the palette when it is changed through ThemeXML:

list.li: -3: The theme's selectionBackground colour, as reflected by SelectBkgd.

description.p: A slot can be redefined at any time. Redefinition changes only the appearance; existing marks and their values are preserved.

Style is not a supported SCIND value.
Indicator is outside the range 8 to 31, or Colour is neither a valid colour nor a theme reference.
The resource has not been initialised

method.name: DefineMarker
method.comment: Defines the appearance of a marker.
method.prototype: ERR sci::DefineMarker(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Marker, SCMK Symbol, struct RGB8 * Fore, struct RGB8 * Bkgd)

input.param: The marker number, from 0 to 24.
The symbol to draw.
The foreground colour. If NULL, the current colour is retained.
The background colour. If NULL, the current colour is retained.

description.p: This method sets the symbol and colours of a marker, which can then be added to lines with AddMarker. Lines that already carry the marker are redrawn with the new definition. Until it is defined, a marker is drawn as a circle with a black outline and a white fill.

Symbols are drawn in the symbol margin in the Bkgd colour, with the outline and any inner sign in the Fore colour. The SCMK::BACKGROUND and SCMK::UNDERLINE symbols are drawn in the text area instead, in the Bkgd colour. If the alpha component of Bkgd is less than 255, these two symbols are blended over the line, which also tints its text. Otherwise they are drawn opaquely beneath the text. The alpha components are ignored for all other symbols.

method.name: DeleteLine
method.comment: Deletes a line.
method.prototype: ERR sci::DeleteLine(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line)

input.param: The number of the line to delete. Indexing starts from 0.

description.p: This method will delete a single line at the position indicated by the Line parameter. If no parameters are provided or the Line parameter is less than zero, the line at the current cursor position will be deleted. If the index exceeds the total number of available lines, the last available line will be targeted.

method.name: ExpandFold
method.comment: Expands a fold without toggling its current state.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ExpandFold(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line)

input.param: Zero-based document line, or -1 for the caret line.

description.p: Expands the fold that starts at Line. If the line does not start a fold, the innermost fold that contains it is expanded. Nested folds keep their own state, so a collapsed child fold remains collapsed. If the fold is hidden within a collapsed ancestor, the ancestors are also expanded so that it becomes visible, and the caret may move to the fold's first line. Expanding a fold that is already expanded and visible succeeds without change.
Unlike ToggleFold, the result does not depend on the fold's current state. Folding must be enabled with FoldingMarkers, and the document needs a Lexer that supports folding.

method.name: FillIndicator
method.comment: Applies an application indicator to a byte range.
method.prototype: ERR sci::FillIndicator(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Indicator, INT Start, INT End, INT Value)

input.param: An indicator slot previously defined with DefineIndicator.
Byte offset of the first byte to mark.
Byte offset immediately after the last byte to mark. Must be between Start and TextLength.
A positive value to associate with the marked bytes. Zero is reserved for unmarked bytes.

description.p: FillIndicator() marks the bytes in the range Start to End with an indicator slot and associates Value with every marked byte. The value is not interpreted by the editor; applications can use it to link a mark to their own data, such as an index into a list of diagnostic messages, and retrieve it later with GetIndicator.

Filling a range overwrites any existing marks of the same slot within that range. Marks in other slots are unaffected, so a byte can carry one value per slot. Marks move with the text when the document is edited, and are trimmed when the text they cover is deleted. Marks are not part of the undo history, so undoing a deletion does not restore them. Offsets are not adjusted to UTF-8 character boundaries.
The slot must have been defined with DefineIndicator. Filling a range does not modify the document, its undo history, DocumentRevision or the selection.

Indicator has not been defined, or Value is not positive.
Indicator is outside the range 8 to 31, or the byte range is invalid.

method.name: FoldAll
method.comment: Expands or collapses every fold, including nested folds.
method.prototype: ERR sci::FoldAll(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Expanded)

input.param: TRUE to expand every fold, FALSE to collapse every fold.

description.p: Applies the same state to every fold in the document. Collapsing marks every fold as collapsed, including folds nested within other folds, so expanding an outer fold afterwards with ExpandFold leaves its children collapsed. Expanding clears all nested collapsed state. Document text, undo history and DocumentRevision are not affected.
Folding must be enabled with FoldingMarkers. If the document contains no folds, the call succeeds and has no effect.

Folding is disabled.

method.name: GetFold
method.comment: Queries a line's containing fold and visibility using current lexer levels.
method.prototype: ERR sci::GetFold(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, INT * Header, INT * Expanded, INT * Visible)

input.param: Zero-based document line, or -1 for the caret line.
Receives the line that starts the fold, or -1 if no fold applies.
Receives TRUE if the fold is expanded, or if no fold applies.
Receives TRUE if the line is visible through all of its enclosing folds.

description.p: Reports the fold that ExpandFold and CollapseFold would act on for Line: the fold that starts at the line, or otherwise the innermost fold that contains it. Fold levels are brought up to date before the query, so the result reflects recent edits. Document text, undo history and DocumentRevision are not affected.

If FoldingMarkers is disabled or no fold applies, Header is -1 and Expanded is TRUE. Visible is independent of Expanded: a line within an expanded fold is still hidden if any enclosing fold is collapsed.

The result is a snapshot. Edits move fold state with the lines of the document and can expand folds around edited text, while changing the Lexer or disabling FoldingMarkers expands every fold. Fold state is not restored automatically after such changes. A client that saves and restores folds must re-evaluate the headers against the current text, then collapse child folds before their parents.

A value is outside of the valid range
The resource has not been initialised
The method was called from within a synchronous editor notification, where fold levels cannot be refreshed.

method.name: GetIndicator
method.comment: Reads the indicator value at a byte position and the extent of its run.
method.prototype: ERR sci::GetIndicator(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Indicator, INT Position, INT * Value, INT * Start, INT * End)
method.tiriPrototype: err, Value:num, Start:num, End:num = GetIndicator(Indicator:num, Position:num)

input.param: An indicator slot previously defined with DefineIndicator.
Byte offset to inspect, from zero to TextLength.
Receives the value at Position, or zero if the byte is not marked.
Receives the byte offset of the first byte in the run.
Receives the byte offset immediately after the last byte in the run.

description.p: GetIndicator() returns the value that FillIndicator associated with the byte at Position, together with the bounds of the contiguous run of bytes that share that value. If the byte is not marked, Value is zero and Start and End describe the surrounding run of unmarked bytes.
Position may equal TextLength, in which case Value is zero and both Start and End are set to Position.
This method is safe to call from notification callbacks.

method.name: GetKeywords
method.comment: Copies a keyword set of the active lexer to a buffer.
method.prototype: ERR sci::GetKeywords(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Set, std::span<int8_t> Buffer)

input.param: Zero-based index of the keyword set to read.
Receives the keyword list as a null-terminated string.

description.p: GetKeywords() copies the keyword list that the active Lexer is currently using for the keyword set Set. The result is the list assigned with SetKeywords if one exists for the active lexer, otherwise it is the lexer's built-in default list, which may be empty.
The number of keyword sets and their meaning depend on the lexer. The buffer must have room for the keyword list and a terminating null byte. If it is too small, the buffer is left unchanged.

input.param: The exact name of the property, as advertised by the active lexer.

description.p: GetLexerProperty() copies the value that SetLexerProperty assigned to the property Name for the active Lexer. If the property is supported but has not been assigned for this lexer, an empty string is returned; the lexer's internal default value is not reported.

The property must be one advertised by the active lexer. The fold and asp.default.language properties are managed by the Scintilla class and cannot be read with this method. The buffer must have room for the value and a terminating null byte. If it is too small, the buffer is left unchanged.

input.param: Line index
Column index

method.name: GetTextRange
method.comment: Copies an exact byte range to a caller-supplied buffer.
method.prototype: ERR sci::GetTextRange(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Start, INT End, std::span<int8_t> Buffer)

input.param: Inclusive byte offset, between zero and TextLength.
Exclusive byte offset, between Start and TextLength. Negative sentinels such as -1 are not supported.
Destination with at least End - Start + 1 bytes of capacity, allowing for the null terminator.

description.p: GetTextRange() copies the document bytes from Start up to, but not including, End into Buffer and appends a terminating null byte. Offsets are byte positions, so a range that splits a multi-byte UTF-8 character is copied as-is. Embedded null bytes in the document are copied verbatim, so use End - Start rather than the null terminator to determine the length of the result.
Unlike GetLine, the range is not limited to a single line and line-end characters are copied without modification. The selection and cursor position are not affected.

method.prototype: ERR sci::GotoLine(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line)

method.comment: Closes the completion list and the call tip.
method.prototype: ERR sci::HidePopups(OBJECTPTR Object)

method.name: InsertText
method.comment: Inserts text into a document.
method.prototype: ERR sci::InsertText(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW String, INT Pos)

input.param: A text string to add.
Byte offset; -1 inserts at the caret and -2 replaces the selection.

description.p: Use InsertText to insert a string at any point in the document (if adding text to the end of the document, we recommend using data channels instead).

method.name: RemoveMarker
method.comment: Removes markers from one line or from the whole document.
method.prototype: ERR sci::RemoveMarker(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, INT Marker)

input.param: The index of the line, or -1 for every line.
The marker number from 0 to 24, or -1 for every marker.

description.p: This method removes a marker that was added with AddMarker. A Line of -1 removes the marker from every line, and a Marker of -1 removes every marker. Removing a marker that is not present is not an error.

method.name: ReplaceLine
method.comment: Replaces a line with new text content.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ReplaceLine(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line, STRVIEW String, INT Length)

input.param: Index of the line being targeted.
The new string that will replace the line.
The number of bytes to replace the target with, or -1 for the entire source string.

description.p: This method will replace an entire line with a new text string. If the new string contains line feeds, then multiple lines will be inserted at the target position. It is possible to limit the number of bytes inserted from the source string by setting the Length parameter. To insert all bytes from the source string, set a Length of -1.

method.name: ReplaceRange
method.comment: Replaces an exact byte range without searching or assigning a selection.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ReplaceRange(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Start, INT End, STRVIEW Text)

input.param: Inclusive byte offset, between zero and TextLength.
Exclusive byte offset, between Start and TextLength. Negative sentinels such as -1 are not supported.
Replacement bytes. An empty string deletes the range. Embedded null bytes are supported.

description.p: ReplaceRange() replaces the document bytes from Start up to, but not including, End with Text. Setting Start and End to the same offset inserts Text at that position, and an empty Text deletes the range. A call with an empty range and an empty Text succeeds without modifying the document.

The replacement is recorded as a single undoable edit, increments DocumentRevision and is reported to ChangeCallback like any other edit. Use BeginUndoAction and EndUndoAction to combine several replacements into one undo step. The current selection is not replaced by Text, although selection and cursor positions after the range are shifted to account for the change in length.
This method is intended for programmatic edits and is not restricted by the SCIF::EDIT flag.

result.error: Operation successful.
The range is invalid, or the replacement would exceed the maximum document length.
The resource has not been initialised
The document is temporarily read-only.
The editor is dispatching a notification and cannot be modified until it returns.
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: ReplaceText
method.comment: Replaces all text within an entire document or limited range.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ReplaceText(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Find, STRVIEW Replace, STF Flags, INT Start, INT End)
method.tiriPrototype: err = ReplaceText(Find:str, Replace:str, Flags:num, Start:num, End:num)

input.param: The keyword string to find.
The string that will replace the keyword.
Optional flags.
The start of the search - set to zero if covering the entire document. If -1, starts from the current cursor position.
The end of the search - set to -1 if covering the entire document.

description.p: The ReplaceText method will replace all instances of the Find string with the content of the Replace string, between a given Start and End point. The STF::CASE, STF::SCAN_SELECTION and STF::EXPRESSION are valid flag options for this method (see FindText for details).

method.name: ScrollToPoint
method.comment: Scrolls the document to a position in the units of the View.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ScrollToPoint(OBJECTPTR Object, INT X, INT Y)

input.param: Horizontal scroll position in the units of the View.
Vertical scroll position in the units of the View.

description.p: This method scrolls the document so that the point (X, Y), measured in the units of the View from the top-left corner of the document, appears at the top-left corner of the View. The Page is moved to (-X, -Y) to reflect the change.
The editor scrolls vertically by whole lines, so Y is rounded to the nearest line. Both coordinates are clamped to the scrollable range of the document.

method.name: SelectRange
method.comment: Selects a range of text, can also deselect all text.
method.prototype: ERR sci::SelectRange(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Start, INT End)

input.param: The anchor byte offset.
The caret byte offset (exclusive for forward selections). A negative value targets the document end.

description.p: Selects a half-open range using zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets. Start is the anchor and End is the caret, so reversed bounds preserve selection direction. Supplying no arguments or two zeroes collapses the selection at the current caret. Existing backend clamping and negative sentinels are preserved.

method.name: SetFont
method.comment: Changes the font that is used for text display.
method.prototype: ERR sci::SetFont(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Face)

input.param: The name of the new font face.

description.p: Call SetFont() to change the font face that is used for displaying text. The Face is a family name as accepted by the Face field, e.g. Source Code Pro or Clean. The current FontSize in pixels is retained.
If the new face is invalid or fails to load, the current font will remain unchanged.

result.error: Operation successful.
The font file could not be loaded.
No matching font could be resolved.
A call to ResolvePath() failed
Failed to resolve the font handle.
Function call missing argument value(s)
Failed to create a new resource

method.name: SetKeywords
method.comment: Replaces a keyword set of the active lexer.
method.prototype: ERR sci::SetKeywords(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Set, STRVIEW Keywords)

input.param: Zero-based index of the keyword set to replace.
Space-separated list of words to use for the set.

description.p: SetKeywords() replaces the keyword list that the active Lexer uses for the keyword set Set. Lexers use keyword sets to classify words, for instance as language keywords or type names, and the number of sets and their meaning depend on the lexer. Some structural lexers, such as Markdown and Diff, have no keyword sets.
Keywords is a complete list of words separated by spaces, and replaces the lexer's built-in default list. An empty string leaves the set empty; it does not restore the default list.

The replacement is stored for the active lexer only, and is reapplied whenever that lexer is selected again. The existing styles are invalidated and recalculated when the text is next drawn; call Colourise to apply the change immediately. The document, its undo history and DocumentRevision are not affected.

result.error: Operation successful.
Keywords contains a null byte.
The active lexer does not provide keyword set Set.
The resource has not been initialised
The editor is dispatching a notification and cannot be modified until it returns.
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: SetLexerProperty
method.comment: Sets a configuration property of the active lexer.
method.prototype: ERR sci::SetLexerProperty(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Name, STRVIEW Value)

input.param: The exact name of the property, as advertised by the active lexer.
The value to assign.

description.p: SetLexerProperty() assigns a value to a property advertised by the active Lexer. Lexer properties adjust how text is classified, for example lexer.json.allow.comments enables comment recognition in the JSON lexer. The available properties depend on the lexer. The fold and asp.default.language properties are managed by the Scintilla class and cannot be set with this method.

Values are validated against the property's type. Boolean properties accept only 0 or 1, and integer properties accept only a decimal integer. String properties accept any value that does not contain a null byte.

The value is stored for the active lexer only. It is removed from the editor when a different lexer is selected, and is reapplied whenever the lexer is selected again. The current value can be read with GetLexerProperty. The existing styles are invalidated and recalculated when the text is next drawn; call Colourise to apply the change immediately.

result.error: Operation successful.
Name or Value contains a null byte, or Value is not valid for the property's type.
Name is not a property advertised by the active lexer, or is reserved.
The resource has not been initialised
The editor is dispatching a notification and cannot be modified until it returns.
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: ShowCallTip
method.comment: Displays a call tip, such as a function signature, below a position in the document.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ShowCallTip(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Pos, CSTRING Text, INT HighlightStart, INT HighlightEnd)

input.param: The document position that the call tip refers to, or -1 for the cursor position.
The text to display.
The byte offset within Text at which highlighting starts.
The byte offset within Text at which highlighting ends. Highlighting is disabled if this does not exceed HighlightStart.

description.p: ShowCallTip() opens a call tip that is attached to Pos. It is typically used to show the parameters of a function while the user types its arguments. Calling ShowCallTip() while a call tip is open replaces it, which is also how the highlighted parameter is updated. Showing a call tip closes the completion list.

The call tip is displayed on the line below Pos, or above it if it would otherwise extend beyond the bottom of the scene. The Text may contain multiple lines that are separated by \n. The characters \001 and \002 are drawn as up and down arrows, which a client can use to let the user cycle through overloads by clicking them. Clicks are reported to the CompletionCallback as SCAC::CALL_TIP_CLICK.

Typing text, moving the cursor left and right, and deleting with Backspace keep the call tip open. It is closed by other cursor movement, Escape, a click in the editor, the loss of the focus, Backspace beyond the cursor position at which it opened, or HidePopups.

method.name: ShowCompletions
method.comment: Displays a list of completion candidates for the word at the cursor.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ShowCompletions(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Length, CSTRING Candidates, SCACF Flags)

input.param: The number of bytes of the typed prefix that precede the cursor.
Completion candidates, separated by line feeds.
Optional flags.

description.p: ShowCompletions() opens the completion list below the word that is being typed, or above it if there is more room there. The Candidates are separated by line feeds and may be given in any order. They are sorted for display and duplicates are removed. The client normally calls ShowCompletions() from the CompletionCallback in response to SCAC::REQUEST or SCAC::CHAR_ADDED.

Length is the number of bytes of the word that precede the cursor and have already been typed. The candidate that begins with this prefix is selected, and the selection follows further typing. If no candidate matches the typed prefix, the list closes. Accepting a candidate replaces the prefix with it. Showing the list closes any call tip.

While the list is open, the Up and Down arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End move the selection. Enter and Tab accept the selected candidate, and Escape closes the list. Tab reaches the editor only if the scene does not use it to cycle the focus, i.e. the scene has the VPF::IGNORE_TAB flag. Other cursor movement, a click in the editor and the loss of the focus also close it. Clicking a candidate selects it, double-clicking accepts it, and the mouse wheel scrolls the list. Acceptance is reported to the CompletionCallback as SCAC::SELECTED and any other closure as SCAC::CANCELLED.
Completions edit the document on the user's behalf, so they require the SCIF::EDIT flag.

method.name: ToggleFold
method.comment: Contracts or expands a fold.
method.prototype: ERR sci::ToggleFold(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Line)

input.param: The index of the line, or -1 for the line of the cursor.

description.p: This method toggles the fold that starts at a line, which hides or shows the lines within the fold. If the line does not start a fold, the innermost fold that contains it is toggled. Folding must be enabled with FoldingMarkers, and the document needs a Lexer that supports folding.

method.name: TrimWhitespace
method.comment: Strips trailing white-space from the document.
method.prototype: ERR sci::TrimWhitespace(OBJECTPTR Object)

description.p: The TrimWhitespace method will remove trailing white-space from every line in the document. Both tabs and spaces are considered white-space - all other characters shall be treated as content.
The position of the cursor is reset to the left margin as a result of calling this method.

field.name: ActivePopup
field.comment: Indicates the code assistance pop-up that is open.

description.p: This read-only field reports SCPOP::COMPLETIONS while the completion list of ShowCompletions is open, SCPOP::CALL_TIP while the call tip of ShowCallTip is open, and SCPOP::NONE otherwise.

field.name: AllowTabs
field.comment: If enabled, use of the tab key produces real tabs and not spaces.

description.p: The Tab key is only received by the editor if the IGNORE_TAB flag is set on its VectorScene. Refer to Focus for details.

field.name: Anchor
field.comment: The main selection anchor as a zero-based UTF-8 byte offset. It may follow CurrentPos.

field.name: AutoIndent
field.comment: If TRUE, enables auto-indenting when the user presses the enter key.

field.name: BkgdColour
field.comment: Defines the background colour. Alpha blending is not supported.

description.p: The BkgdColour applies to the text area and to all lexer styles. The margins use their own colours.

field.name: CanRedo
field.comment: Reports whether the backend has an undone edit available to redo.

field.name: CanUndo
field.comment: Reports whether the backend has an edit available to undo.

field.name: ChangeCallback
field.comment: Receives an ordered stream of document byte changes after editing completes.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to receive a record of every insertion and deletion of text. The prototype for the callback function is Function(*Scintilla, struct(*ScintillaChange) Change). Each ScintillaChange structure describes one change:

Every change is reported, whether it originates from user input, the clipboard, programmatic methods such as ReplaceRange, file loading, undo or redo. Each record corresponds to exactly one increment of DocumentRevision, and records are delivered in the order that the changes occurred without being coalesced. A client that starts with a copy of the document can therefore replay the stream to keep an exact mirror of the text. An edit that replaces existing text is reported as a deletion followed by an insertion. Edits made inside an undo group are reported individually.
Delivery is deferred to the next cycle of message processing, after the editing call has returned. Edits made from within the callback are queued and delivered after the current batch completes.

Changes made while no callback is defined are not recorded. Setting, replacing or clearing the callback discards any records that have not yet been delivered, including the remainder of a batch in progress. If a script callback raises an error, the callback is cleared and its undelivered records are discarded.
The Change structure is only valid for the duration of the callback, so C++ clients must copy any values that need to be retained. Script clients receive their own copy of the record.

field.name: CompletionCallback
field.comment: Reports the events that relate to code completion and call tips.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to provide completion candidates and call tips. The prototype for the callback function is Function(*Scintilla, SCAC Event, INT Position, INT Value, CSTRING Text).
The Event is one of the following:

SCAC::REQUEST and SCAC::CHAR_ADDED are reported as they occur, so the client can respond with ShowCompletions or ShowCallTip. Position is the cursor position, and for SCAC::CHAR_ADDED the Value is the Unicode code point of the character that was typed. The client usually examines the text that precedes the cursor to choose its candidates. Ctrl+Space is reported only while the editor has the SCIF::EDIT flag.

SCAC::SELECTED, SCAC::CANCELLED and SCAC::CALL_TIP_CLICK are reported on the next cycle of message processing, after the editor has completed the operation. For SCAC::SELECTED, the Text is the accepted candidate and Position is the start of the replaced text, and the candidate has already been inserted. For SCAC::CALL_TIP_CLICK, Position is the position that the call tip refers to. The Text is empty for every event other than SCAC::SELECTED.

field.name: CurrentPos
field.comment: The main selection caret as a zero-based UTF-8 byte offset.

field.name: CursorCol
field.comment: The current column of the text cursor.

description.p: The CursorCol and CursorRow fields reflect the current row and column of the user's text cursor. Use EventCallback and listen for the event SEF::CURSOR_POS to receive updates on changes to CursorCol and CursorRow.

field.name: CursorColour
field.comment: Defines the colour of the text cursor. Alpha blending is not supported.

field.name: CursorRow
field.comment: The current row of the text cursor.

description.p: The CursorCol and CursorRow fields reflect the current row and column of the user's text cursor. Use EventCallback and listen for the event SEF::CURSOR_POS to receive updates on changes to CursorCol and CursorRow.

field.name: DocumentRevision
field.comment: Monotonically increasing revision of document text.

description.p: The DocumentRevision value starts at zero and is incremented for every insertion or deletion of text, including edits made by the user, programmatic changes, undo, redo and the loading of new content. Styling, folding and selection changes do not affect the revision. The value is never decremented, so undoing an edit does not restore an earlier revision.

Clients can record the revision when caching information about the document, then compare it later to determine whether the text may have changed in the interim. Each change reported to ChangeCallback carries the revision reached after that change in its Revision value.

field.name: EOLMode
field.comment: Line-ending policy for newly entered keyboard and clipboard text.

description.p: Determines the line ending inserted when the user presses Enter, and the line endings applied to pasted and dropped text. Rectangular copies also end each row with this line ending. The default is LF on every platform.

Changing this field does not modify existing text; use ConvertEOLs to normalise it. Text supplied through String, ReplaceText and other programmatic operations keeps its original line endings, as does text loaded from a file. Loading does not detect or change this setting, so applications that want to match a file's line endings must inspect the text and set EOLMode explicitly. SaveToObject writes the document bytes without conversion.

field.name: EventCallback
field.comment: Provides callbacks for global state changes.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to receive event notifications. It must be set in conjunction with EventFlags so that you can select the type of notifications that will be received.
The callback function must be in the format Function(*Scintilla, INT64 EventFlag).
The EventFlag value will indicate the event that occurred. Please see the EventFlags field for a list of supported events and additional details.

field.name: EventFlags
field.comment: Specifies events that need to be reported from the Scintilla object.

description.p: To receive event notifications, set EventCallback with a function reference and the EventFlags field with a mask that indicates the events that need to be received.

field.name: Face
field.comment: The font family used for drawing and measuring document text.

description.p: Accepts a font family name supported by the vector module's GetFontHandle() function, including bitmap faces such as Clean. The default is Source Code Pro. Regular, bold, italic and bold italic styles share this family and FontSize. Set this field before or after initialisation. Changing it reloads the styles and updates layout and margins. SetFont provides the same operation. A failed resolution preserves the current face and handles.
This field and FontSize replace the former Font object field; scripts must use these fields to customise fonts.

field.name: FileDrop
field.comment: A callback for receiving drag and drop file notifications.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to receive the paths of files that the user drops onto the editor. The prototype for the callback function is Function(*Scintilla, CSTRING Path). The callback is called once for each dropped file, in the order provided by the drag source.

The editor accepts file drops only while this field is set, so leave it undefined if files are not to be dropped onto the editor. The editor does not act on the dropped files; it is the responsibility of the client to open, load or insert them as required. File drops do not require the SCIF::EDIT flag, but are refused while the editor is disabled. When a drag source offers both files and text, the files are preferred and the text is not inserted.
Delivery is cancelled if the document is modified between the drop and the arrival of the data. If the callback destroys the editor, the remaining paths are not reported.
Drag and drop requires the hosting VectorScene to have VPF::DROP_TARGETS set.

field.name: Flags
field.comment: Optional flags.

field.name: Focus
field.comment: Defines the viewport that is monitored for user focus changes.

description.p: The editor has the user focus while the Focus viewport or any of its children has the focus. Keyboard input is received from the Focus viewport during that time, and the caret is shown and blinks. If not set prior to initialisation, the Viewport is used. Clicking within the editor gives the focus to one of its internal viewports, which are children of the Viewport.

Keyboard input requires a VectorScene that is linked to a Surface. The scene uses the Tab key to move the focus between keyboard subscribers unless its IGNORE_TAB flag is set, in which case the Tab key reaches the editor.

field.name: FoldingMarkers
field.comment: Enables code folding and shows the fold margin.

description.p: Set this field to true to enable code folding. Folding is computed by the active Lexer, so a document without a lexer, or with a lexer that does not support folding, has no folds. The fold margin is shown to the left of the text and marks each fold with a box that contains a plus (contracted) or minus (expanded) sign. Clicking the box of a fold toggles it. Folds can also be toggled with ToggleFold.

The lines of a contracted fold are hidden. They are shown again if the fold is expanded, if the cursor is moved into them with GotoLine or SelectRange, or if they are edited. Setting FoldingMarkers to false expands every fold.

field.name: FontSize
field.comment: The font em size in pixels.

description.p: Sets a positive integer pixel size for every text style. The default is 14 pixels. This is not a point size and is independent of display density. The size is expressed in the units of the View, so the fonts are loaded at the size multiplied by the device scale of the host, rounded to whole pixels. Bitmap faces select their nearest supported point size and are not scaled. Set this field before or after initialisation. Changing it reloads the font handles and updates layout and margins.

field.name: IndentWidth
field.comment: Indentation width in fixed-width character columns, independently of tab stops.

description.p: Sets the width of one indentation level, which determines how far keyboard indentation commands indent and outdent lines and the spacing of IndentationGuides. This allows indentation to differ from TabWidth, which continues to control tab stops; for example, a width of 4 with tab stops at 8. AllowTabs determines whether indentation is written with tab characters. The default of 0 uses the TabWidth value. Valid values range from 0 to 200.
AutoIndent is not affected, and continues to copy the leading whitespace of the previous line. Changing this field does not modify existing whitespace.

field.name: IndentationGuides
field.comment: Controls the display of indentation guides without changing document text.

description.p: Indentation guides are vertical lines drawn at each indentation level, spaced by IndentWidth or by TabWidth if IndentWidth is zero. Modes that infer the indentation of blank lines also use the indentation behaviour of the active Lexer. The setting is retained when the lexer or theme changes. The default is NONE.

field.name: LeftMargin
field.comment: The amount of white-space at the left side of the page.

description.p: The margin is expressed in the units of the View, and is scaled with the content if the host is scaled.

field.name: Lexer
field.comment: The lexer for document styling is defined here.

description.p: The lexer can be changed at any time. Its keyword lists and semantic style colours are refreshed immediately. Existing folds are expanded and folding remains enabled if FoldingMarkers is set. Set the lexer to zero to display plain text. ASP uses the HTML lexer with VBScript server blocks; Tiri keywords follow the parser's reserved words.

If the DETECT_LEXER flag is set, the lexer is chosen from the file name whenever a file is loaded, and this overrides any existing value. The Lexer is left unchanged if the file name does not match a known type.

field.name: LexerName
field.comment: Selects the lexer by name.

description.p: LexerName is a name-based alternative to the Lexer field. Reading it returns the canonical name of the active lexer, and writing it selects the lexer with the matching name, with the same effect as setting Lexer. The list of valid names can be read from SupportedLexers. Names are case-sensitive.

The aliases lua, hypertext and none are accepted for tiri, html and null respectively, but the field always reports the canonical name. Writing an unknown name fails with ERR::NoSupport and leaves the active lexer unchanged. The lexer cannot be changed while the editor is dispatching a notification.

field.name: LineCount
field.comment: The total number of lines in the document.

field.name: LineHighlight
field.comment: The colour to use when highlighting the line that contains the user's cursor.

description.p: The highlight is shown while the editor has the focus. An alpha value of zero disables it. An opaque colour is drawn beneath the text, while a translucent colour is blended over the line, which also tints its text. Translucent colours blend in the same way as a translucent vector fill, i.e. with the gamma-correct blending of the Vector module, so a 50% colour appears lighter than an average of the sRGB values.

field.name: LineNumbers
field.comment: Line numbers will appear on the left when this value is TRUE.

field.name: MarginClick
field.comment: A callback for receiving clicks in the symbol and fold margins.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to receive notifications when the user clicks in the symbol margin or the fold margin. This is typically used to toggle breakpoints or bookmarks with AddMarker and RemoveMarker. The prototype for the callback function is Function(*Scintilla, SCMG Margin, INT Line, KQ Qualifiers).

The Margin is SCMG::SYMBOLS or SCMG::FOLDING, and the Line is the index of the line that was clicked. The Qualifiers indicate the modifier keys that were held, as a combination of KQ::SHIFT, KQ::CTRL and KQ::ALT. Modifier keys are only known while the editor has the user focus.

A click in the fold margin has already toggled the fold of the line (if it is a fold header) when the callback is made. While MarginClick is defined, a click in the symbol margin is reported instead of selecting the line. Clicks in the line number margin always select the line and are not reported.

field.name: Modified
field.comment: Returns true if the document has been modified and not saved.

description.p: The Modified field controls the modification state of the document. It is automatically changed to a value of TRUE when the user edits the document. To receive notification of changes to the document state, you should subscribe to the Modified field.
It is recommended that you manually set this field to false if the document is saved to disk. The Scintilla class will not make this change for you automatically.

field.name: Origin
field.comment: Sets the Path field without loading the document.

description.p: Setting the Origin will update Path without updating the content of the Scintilla object. Use for situations such as changing the document location or name.

field.name: Page
field.comment: An internally created viewport that represents the extent of the document.

description.p: The Page is created on initialisation as a child of the View. It represents the virtual extent of the document, and scrolling is achieved by moving the Page within the View. The Page can be referenced as the page of a scrollbar.

The editor manages the size of the Page. Its height allows the last line of the document to be scrolled to the bottom of the View, and its width allows the longest line to be scrolled into view. If the Page is moved by a third party, the editor scrolls to match and then snaps the Page to the nearest whole line.

field.name: Path
field.comment: Identifies the location of a text file to load.

description.p: To load data from a text file into a scintilla object, set the Path field.

If the Path is set after initialisation, the existing content will be cleared and data loaded from the location that you specify. To change the path without automatically loading from the source file, set the Origin field instead.

field.name: RightMargin
field.comment: Defines the amount of white-space at the right side of the page.

description.p: The margin is expressed in the units of the View, and is scaled with the content if the host is scaled.

field.name: SelectBkgd
field.comment: Defines the background colour of selected text. Supports alpha blending.

description.p: An alpha value of zero disables the selection background. An opaque colour is drawn beneath the selected text. A translucent colour is blended over the selection after the text is drawn, in the same way as LineHighlight, so that the text remains visible through it. Consider disabling SelectFore with a translucent background so that the selected text retains its styled colours.
The background of the main selection is affected. The additional rows of a rectangular selection use Scintilla's default colour for additional selections.

field.name: SelectFore
field.comment: Defines the colour of selected text.

description.p: Selected text is drawn in this colour, overriding the colours of its style. An alpha value of zero disables the override. Other alpha values are ignored and the colour is drawn opaquely.

field.name: SelectedText
field.comment: Retrieves the contiguous byte span of the main selection.

description.p: Returns the document bytes between the start and end of the main selection. If the selection is empty, an empty string is returned. When multiple or rectangular selections are active, only the main selection range is returned and additional ranges are ignored. Line-end characters within the selection are returned without modification.

field.name: SelectionEnd
field.comment: The exclusive upper byte offset of the main selection, independent of direction.

field.name: SelectionStart
field.comment: The lower byte offset of the main selection, independent of selection direction.

field.name: ShowWhitespace
field.comment: White-space characters will be visible to the user when this field is TRUE.

field.name: String
field.comment: Manages the text data as a complete string.

description.p: A Scintilla document can be completely updated by setting the String field. Equally, the entire document can be retrieved by getting the String field. Please be aware that retrieving the document in string format can be very inefficient, as the document text is normally stored on a per-line basis. Consider using the GetLine method as the preferred alternative, as it is much more efficient with memory usage.

field.name: SupportedLexers
field.comment: Lists the names of all supported lexers. This field is read-only.

description.p: Returns the canonical name of every lexer that can be assigned to LexerName, separated by newline characters. The list includes null, which selects plain text. The content of the list is fixed for the lifetime of the process.

field.name: Symbols
field.comment: Shows the symbol margin, in which markers are displayed.

description.p: Set this field to true to show the symbol margin to the left of the text. The margin displays the markers that are added to lines with AddMarker. While the margin is hidden, a line that carries markers is highlighted with their background colour instead. Markers that highlight the text itself, such as SCMK::BACKGROUND, are displayed regardless of this setting.
If MarginClick is defined, clicks in the symbol margin are reported to it. Otherwise a click in the margin selects the line, as it does in the line number margin.

field.name: TabWidth
field.comment: The width of tab stops in the document, measured as fixed-width characters.

field.name: TextColour
field.comment: Defines the default colour of foreground text. Alpha blending is not supported.

description.p: TextColour applies to plain text, identifiers and any unclassified styles. Configure lexer and margin colours through ThemeXML. Theme colours are stored independently for each editor and are retained across lexer changes.
The defaults are a white background, black text and operators, grey comments, firebrick keywords, dark red strings, blue numbers, green directives and violet types.

field.name: TextLength
field.comment: The document length in bytes, including tabs, CR and LF bytes. An empty document has length zero.

field.name: ThemeXML
field.comment: Applies colours from a preconfigured XML object. This field is write-only.

description.p: Assign an initialised XML object containing one theme element with one palette child. The palette's attributes specify SVG colour strings:
description.pre: <theme> <palette background="#232a37" text="white" keyword="#70b8ff" comment="#99aabb" string="#b5d99c" number="#d4a5ff" operator="white" preprocessor="#b5d99c" type="#ffc080" error="#ff8899" margin="#99aabb" marginBackground="#303745" cursor="white" lineHighlight="transparent" selectionForeground="white" selectionBackground="#335588"/> </theme>
description.p: The theme element accepts no attributes, and the palette accepts no child elements or non-whitespace text. All palette attributes are optional and case-sensitive. Omitted colours retain their current values. Hex colours, SVG colour names and colour functions such as rgb() and oklch() are accepted. Gradients, painter lists and unknown attributes are rejected. Alpha is ignored except for lineHighlight and selection colours, where zero disables the corresponding highlight or selection override. Translucent lineHighlight and selectionBackground colours blend over the text, as described for LineHighlight and SelectBkgd. Other alpha values produce opaque colours.

The colours are copied during assignment and the XML object is not retained or modified. Assigning before initialisation configures the initial colours; assigning afterwards repaints without changing text, selection or contracted folds. Invalid themes leave all colours unchanged.

field.name: View
field.comment: An internally created viewport that clips the visible content of the editor.

description.p: The View is created on initialisation as a child of the Viewport, and covers its entire area. It represents the visible window into the document and clips the Page. The View can be referenced as the view of a scrollbar, which may reduce the size of the View by changing its XOffset and YOffset values.

field.name: Viewport
field.comment: The viewport that will host the editor.

description.p: This compulsory field refers to the VectorViewport that will host the editor's graphics. If not set prior to initialisation, the Scintilla object's owner will be used if it is a VectorViewport.

field.name: Wordwrap
field.comment: Enables automatic word wrapping when TRUE.
